newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX PV power races to new highs on heat, outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX PV power races to new highs on heat, outages.

text.p: NYMEX Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures Thursday rose to new life-of-contract highs on a combination of power plant outages, strong natural gas prices and forecasts of lingering heat in Southwest.
"It's all driven by PV with the weather and the outages which caught some people off guard," said a Northwest trader.

Following a handful of unplanned shutdowns of several fossil-fired plants in California and the Southwest, PV prices were given more bullish news when Southern California Edison Co pushed back the restart of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in San Clemente, Calif., to July 10 from late June for additional work, brokers and traders said.
July PV settled up $3.04 at $35.70 megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a new contract high at $36.25 and opening a price gap at $33.75-35.70.
August PV finished up $2.24 at $35.80 after setting new contract high also at $36.25, while deferred PV months ended 20 to 78 cents higher.
Market sources said PV's strength pulled California-Oregon Border (COB) futures higher.
July COB settled up $2.13 at $22.23 a MWh, still below its contract high of $24.75.
August COB finished at $1.46 at $24.44. Other COB contracts ended flat to 95 cents higher.
So far this week, July PV gained $8.02 or up 29 percent from Friday, and July COB $4.43 or 25 percent.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at PV rose $3-4 to $32.00-35.00, while those at COB held steady at $19.50-20.00.
In other outage news, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners, New Mexico, coal-fired plant may be shut for a week after it tripped off-line Wednesday due to a tube rupture,

Several units which were shut for unexpected maintenance were scheduled to return to service soon including the 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada, and two 750 MW units at the Moss Landing natural gas-fired power plant near Monterey, Calif..
The 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was tentatively set to restart next Wednesday or Thursday, pending approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

The bullish tone on power futures was also underpinned by a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee plan to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan still requires the approval of the WSCC board.
Higher air-conditioning demand in the West also pushed up the region's natural gas prices.
June gas deliveries at San Juan/Blanco Hub rose five cents to $2.06-2.09 per million British thermal units, while July prices climbed about six cents to $1.98-1.99 per mmBtu.
NYMEX estimated a record volume for COB at 1,189 contracts and for PV at 1,228.
Brokers and brokers said today's momentum would likely carry the complex to new highs Friday despite signs that the market may be overvalued.
"It's really tough to say. It's looks like a good sell here, but I'm not surprised if it'll go up again," said a Houston futures trader.
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
